author: tools-tooltips-architecture
purpose: Proposes the Studio tool palette, the tool-options surface, the tooltip and help system, the tooltip/parameter data contract, discoverability at 40k-capability scale, and the accessibility naming scheme. Every quantity in the analysis section was computed from the parsed green-room captures; nothing is recalled.

method.tool_list_construction: The capability registry's kind=='tool' bucket (1,270 rows) was inspected and REJECTED as the basis for the tool surface: every one of its 1,270 rows lists affinity as a source app, and for the other apps it is dominated by option-value strings misclassified as tools (figma's 47 'tool' rows are Auto, Bevel, Bold, Both, Bottom, Hue, Italic, Multiply...). The distinct tool list below was therefore rebuilt from primary per-app tool registries.

method.deduplication: 527 raw names normalised (vendor prefix stripped, trailing 'Tool' stripped, Colour->Color, punctuation folded, lowercased) then collapsed through an explicit 240-entry cross-vendor synonym table (Eyedropper/Colour Picker/Color Sampler/Sampler -> color picker; Scroll/Grabber Hand/Liquify Hand/Pan -> hand; Clone Stamp -> clone brush; Magnify -> zoom; Freehand -> pencil; and so on). method.honesty_note: The synonym table is authored judgement over parsed names, and is the only non-mechanical step in the count. It is shipped inline in the artifact via vendor_variants on every row so any merge can be audited and reversed.

tool_families.definition: Pick, sub-pick and group-pick whole objects, nodes and clips.
Produce or refine a pixel / range / colour selection rather than picking an object.
Move the viewport. Never mutates the document.
Deposit colour with a stroke, raster or vector.
Remove coverage with a stroke.
Replace image content from elsewhere, from a model, or from a computed reconstruction.
Modify tone, colour, focus or a live adjustment by painting a mask.
Construct and manipulate curve geometry and its nodes, handles and topology.
Parametric primitive construction, from rectangle to cog to three-point circle.
Create and edit text runs, frames, paths-on-type, grids and tables.
Apply and sample fills, gradients, meshes, transparency and styles.
Define the document, page, artboard, slice, frame and placement geometry.
Move, scale, rotate, distort, liquify and remap existing geometry or pixels.
Sample distances, counts, notes and alignment without changing render output.
Author and edit masks, mattes and source-image masks as first-class targets.
Affinity models each non-destructive tonal/colour adjustment as a selectable tool, not only a menu item.
Affinity models each non-destructive filter (blur, sharpen, distort, stylise) as a selectable tool.
Model-backed tools: generative fill / expand / extend, background removal, ML selection.
Premiere's trim grammar: ripple, roll, slip, slide, rate stretch, razor, track select, remix.
Illustrator's symbolism set: spray and then modify instances in place.
Chart construction tools that build geometry from a data table.

family_grouping_notes.why_21: 21 is the smallest grouping in which every family has a single-sentence definition that a user can act on, and no family exceeds 46 members. It is also browsable in one screen, which 353 is not.
family_grouping_notes.two_families_are_a_vendor_artefact: adjustment_live (36) and filter_live (44), 80 tools between them and 22.7% of the whole list, exist because Affinity models every non-destructive adjustment and every live filter as a SELECTABLE TOOL as well as a menu command. Photoshop and Illustrator model the same operations as menu items or adjustment layers only. Studio must take a position: if these stay tools, the palette gains 80 slots that no other vendor puts there; if they become commands, 80 rows leave the tool surface and the deduplicated palette drops to 273. This is flagged as an open question, not decided here.
family_grouping_notes.assignment_method: Family assignment is an ordered regex over the canonical name, followed by a 33-entry manual correction pass for cases where an earlier pattern fired first (for example 'ripple edit' matching the transform pattern 'ripple' before the timeline rule, 'procedural texture' matching the type pattern on the substring 'text', and 'baseline grid' / 'frame grid' matching the shape pattern 'grid' although they are typographic guides). The corrections are listed in the artifact's own history rather than hidden: every distinct_tools row carries its final family, and every family lists its members, so any disagreement is inspectable without re-running the extraction.

tooltip_text_coverage.headline: At the TOOL level the green room is poor: at most 59.5% of the 353 distinct tools have a recoverable vendor-written sentence, and 0% of those sentences are mechanically bound to a tool name. At the CONTROL level it is rich: 78-86% of controls and parameters carry vendor text.

tools_with_a_recoverable_vendor_sentence.basis: Affinity's string table holds 212 distinct explanatory sentences under the [Tool summary] / [Tool description] contexts. Affinity is the ONLY captured application that ships per-tool prose.

tools_with_a_MECHANICALLY_BOUND_sentence.blocker: Serif's .NET resource keys are the neutral English source text plus a bracketed context, e.g. 'Bloom Tool [Tool description]' and 'Apply a soft diffusion of light effect. [Tool summary]'. Nothing in the resource file joins the two. The join key does not exist in the shipped strings. Same class of defect as the tool_panel_registry's own admission that id_to_name_binding is 'unresolved'.

tools_proven_to_have_NO_vendor_prose.basis: 57 strings appear under BOTH [Tool description] and [Tool summary] with the tool's own name as the value. Affinity fell back to the name where no summary was written. Those 57 tools demonstrably have no descriptive sentence.

tools_with_a_name_keyed_ui_vocabulary_bu.basis: 431 tool-scoped context buckets were recovered from the Affinity string table ('Pen tool reflection', 'Node tool context toolbar control tooltip', 'Fill Tool Context Toolbar Control Text' ...). 192 of the 353 canonical tools match one by name token. These pin a tool's OPTION SET even where they do not describe the tool.

where_the_gaps_are: The 353-tool list is name-rich and prose-poor. Any plan that assumes tooltips can be generated for tools is wrong: it can be generated for at most 59.5% and bound for 0% until the Affinity name<->summary join is recovered.

The five families with zero cross-app overlap (mask_channel, generative_ml, timeline_edit, symbol_instance, data_graph, 36 tools) are sourced from a single vendor each, so a single capture gap wipes out the whole family's prose.

Premiere contributes 39 tools and zero labels. Every timeline_edit tool name in this artifact was decoded from a command id (cmd.tools.03ripple -> Ripple Edit), which is parsed but not vendor-labelled.
Figma and After Effects contribute no tools and no tool prose at all.

The tool class that loads 'Bloom Tool [Tool description]' is the same class that loads its summary. That join is present in the IL even though it is absent from the string table.
proposed_unblock.expected_yield: lifts tool-level bound prose from 0% to roughly 58% (205 of 353), and would also resolve the 143 4CC tool ids the tool_panel_registry left unresolved
proposed_unblock.cost: one extraction microtask; the assembly is already decompiled for the string pass

tool_options_patterns.surface: Options bar (horizontal, under the menu bar, full width)
tool_options_patterns.what_changes_on_tool_select: The whole bar is replaced by that tool's modal parameters. A tool preset picker sits at the far left as a permanent affordance.

captured_evidence.detail: Photoshop also ships 3 TASKSPACES (Select and Mask: 8 tools / 15 properties; Content-Aware Fill: 6 tools / 5 properties; Neural Filters: 5 tools / 0). A taskspace is a scoped tool+option set entered from a command, not a persona: it does not swap the panel layout, the menu, or the rest of the application.

tool_options_patterns.significance_for_studio: The taskspace is the correct precedent for the one legitimate case of tool-set reduction. It is job-scoped, document-scoped, and exits.

tool_options_patterns.surface: Control bar (horizontal), plus 559 EVE dialog layouts for anything larger
tool_options_patterns.what_changes_on_tool_select: Control bar shows the tool's own parameters; anything with more than a row of controls opens as an EVE-described dialog.
tool_options_patterns.significance_for_studio: Adobe's own dialog description language separates the SLIDER range from the EDIT range on 11 controls, 9 of which actually differ. That is the soft/hard bound distinction, present in a shipped declarative format.

tool_options_patterns.surface: Context toolbar (horizontal), plus a settings flyout for overflow
tool_options_patterns.what_changes_on_tool_select: The context toolbar is rebuilt from the tool's declared control set, and the tool's 'reflected properties' are pushed into the panels.

captured_evidence.overflow_mechanism: [Tool settings flyout] (14 strings) and [Tool settings flyout group heading] (4 strings)

tool_options_patterns.significance_for_studio: Affinity's own worst case is 81 context-toolbar strings on ONE tool (Select). A single horizontal row cannot hold that, and Affinity solves it with a grouped flyout, not by truncating.

tool_options_patterns.surface: Effect Controls PANEL (vertical, dockable) - not a bar
tool_options_patterns.what_changes_on_selection: The panel is rebuilt from the selected clip's effect stack; each effect contributes a collapsible group of parameters.

lumetri.example: Temperature hard[-150,150] ui[-100,100]; Exposure hard[-7,7] ui[-5,5]

captured_evidence.toolpanel_note: a command cmd.toolpanel.wingtip.place_in_options_bar exists, so Premiere itself has an options-bar concept bolted onto its tool panel

tool_options_patterns.significance_for_studio: Once a parameter set exceeds roughly a dozen controls it stops being a bar and becomes a panel. Premiere proves it, Lumetri proves the group mechanism, and the soft/hard bound split appears again.

tool_options_patterns.surface: Effect Controls panel; parameter structure declared in the plug-in binary
tool_options_patterns.what_changes_on_selection: The panel renders the effect's declared parameter records in declaration order, honouring group and collapse flags.

captured_evidence.example: 'Blend': valid[5, 10000] but slider[10, 500], default 100, precision 1 - the typed range is 20x the drag range

tool_options_patterns.significance_for_studio: This is the single highest-quality parameter source in the entire green room. It carries every field OUI-008 asks for: hard bounds, separate soft bounds, default, decimal precision, unit, display flags, enumerated options, group boundaries and a collapsed-by-default flag.

tool_options_patterns.what_changes_on_selection: The control panel switches on what is selected (object vs text vs table vs frame), not on which tool is active.
tool_options_patterns.significance_for_studio: InDesign already separates 'what the tool will do' from 'what the selection is', and puts the second on the shared bar.

tool_options_patterns.surface: Property inspectors - 60 of them, dispatched by selection
tool_options_patterns.what_changes_on_selection: The host asks each inspector canInspectSelection() and shows the highest-priority match.
tool_options_patterns.significance_for_studio: THE key find. A shipped application already implements exactly what the operator asked for: per-element declarative availability (enabler_js), declarative visibility (showif_js), a named invalidation event (update_event), a stable id, and a resolved tooltip string - all on the same record. Availability by context, not by mode, is not a new idea to be invented; it is 25-year-old field-proven Adobe infrastructure.

tool_options_patterns.surface: Right-hand module panel stack, grouped by concern
tool_options_patterns.what_changes_on_tool_select: Selecting Crop / Healing / Masking expands that tool's own panel in place inside the stack.
tool_options_patterns.significance_for_studio: Panel-in-stack is a third valid options placement, and the one that suits photo work where the tool's options are long-lived rather than per-gesture.

persona_evidence.claim: The captures contain no vendor that gates tools by persona except Affinity, and Affinity itself ships a parallel JOB-based mechanism that does the same work better.

affinity.note: each .afstudio carries its own name, a prose desc, a tool-panel group list and a panel shelf layout

shipped_workspaces_are_all_job_named.finding: 42 shipped workspaces across four vendors. Every single one is named for a JOB or a TASK. Not one is named for a persona, a discipline or an application mode.

affinity_persona_toolbars_are_thin.reading: The persona toolbars carry command sets (align, distribute, boolean geometry, mesh/mask management), not tool sets. The persona toggle's real payload is a handful of context commands wrapped in a full-application mode switch.

tool_level.worked_example: Crop is present in affinity, illustrator, indesign, lightroom_classic and photoshop. Pen, Hand, Zoom, Line, Ellipse, Rectangle and Polygon are each present in five. Under persona gating those eight tools are implemented once and then hidden four to five times over, and the user must know which mode owns the copy they want.

cost_of_gating.conclusion: Persona gating converts a one-time implementation into a permanent lookup problem for the user and a permanent visibility matrix for the implementer.

photoshop_precedent.claim_checked: The operator's point that Photoshop historically shipped pen, vector and video tools in one application is supported by the capture.
photoshop_precedent.evidence: Photoshop's single .kys tool table contains, side by side and with no mode gate: Pen Tool, Freeform Pen Tool, Convert Point Tool, Add/Delete Anchor Point Tool, Path Selection Tool, Direct Selection Tool, Rectangle/Ellipse/Polygon/Line/Custom Shape Tool, Horizontal and Vertical Type Tool, Frame Tool, Artboard Tool, Slice and Slice Select Tool, plus the full raster set. 92 entries, one flat namespace, one keyboard-shortcut context.

tool_palette_model.shape: A single-column vertical rail on the left edge of the Studio viewport, holding one slot per available TOOL GROUP. Not a persona switcher, not a mode, not a ribbon.

grouping.rule: A tool group is a set of tools that share a family AND are mutually exclusive alternatives for the same gesture. Family is the taxonomic axis (21 families); group is the ergonomic axis (one slot).
grouping.example: family=select_region contains 22 tools; those become four groups: Marquee (rect/ellipse/row/column), Lasso (freehand/polygonal/magnetic), Magic Selection (magic wand, quick selection, object selection, selection brush), Selection Refine (feather/grow-shrink/smooth/outline/refine).
grouping.why_not_one_slot_per_family: navigate has 4 tools and filter_live has 35. A slot per family makes one slot trivial and another a menu.

visible_at_rest.evidence: Affinity's nine shipped workspaces declare 5, 15, 18, 18, 18, 19, 20, 23 and 25 tool-panel groups (median 18) while carrying 4 to 97 tools. Photoshop's palette is ~23 slots over ~70 tools. Illustrator is ~24 slots over 87. Every shipped reference lands between 18 and 25; 20 sits in the middle of the observed band.
visible_at_rest.consequence: 20 visible slots must reach 353 tools. They cannot and must not try. Roughly 120 tools live in the rail's groups; the remaining ~230 are reached by context, search or family browse. That is the honest architecture, and it is what all three references actually do.

nesting_position.verdict: REJECT the timed long-press as the only path to a variant. KEEP an untimed, visible disclosure. Retain long-press as a muscle-memory alias only.
reasoning: A timed press is an invisible gesture with a hidden duration. Nothing on screen states it exists or how long it takes.

It is hostile to the out-of-process GUI inspector: a timed press is nondeterministic to drive and flaky to assert. Handshake validates GUI work through that inspector, so a gesture the inspector cannot reliably produce is a gesture the product cannot reliably test.
It costs the long-press latency on every single variant switch, in the hands of a user who switches variants constantly.
Adobe itself already ships two untimed alternatives (Shift+key cycling, and the tool preset picker), which is an admission that the flyout alone is insufficient.
mechanism: Every group slot with more than one member renders a persistent corner marker. The group is visible at rest, not discovered by accident.
Untimed path 1: click the marker, or secondary-click anywhere on the slot. The variant strip opens immediately with no timer.

Untimed path 2: press the group's shortcut repeatedly to cycle members. Photoshop already classifies this in its own shortcut file - conflicts.within_scope entries are labelled tool_cycle_group, 'multiple tools sharing one letter is Photoshop's documented tool-cycle behaviour'.
Untimed path 3: type the tool name into tool search or the command palette and get the tool directly, never touching the rail.
Long-press is accepted as an alias for path 1 with identical result and no distinct behaviour. It is never load-bearing.
The last-used member of a group becomes the slot's face. The palette adapts to the user without any mode, persona or preference.
nesting_position.group_size_evidence: Across Affinity's nine workspaces the tool-group size histogram is: 93 groups of 1, 18 of 2, 8 of 3, 4 of 4, 9 of 5, 1 of 6, 2 of 13 and 5 of 24. The 24-member groups (the shapes group) are not usable as a flyout strip; they need the family browse path, which is why the browse surface below is not optional.

availability_rule.statement: A tool's presence and enablement in the palette is a pure function of (document.kind, active_layer.kind, selection.kind, active_task_scope) evaluated against that tool's declared requires predicate. No global mode, persona, workspace, preference or persona-like toggle may add or remove a tool. A workspace may only REORDER and PRIORITISE what the predicate already permits; it may never gate.
availability_rule.prior_art: Directly generalised from Dreamweaver's shipped toolbar records, which carry enabler_js (48 of 85 items), showif_js (15), update_event (64) and dom_required (57) per item, and from its 60 property inspectors, every one of which implements canInspectSelection and declares binds_to_tag + priority + selection_scope.

context_vector.document.color_mode: rgb | cmyk | grayscale | lab | indexed | hdr
context_vector.note: layer.kind is drawn from the registry's 400 document_primitives; document.kind from its 17 domains.

three_valued_result.AVAILABLE: Predicate true. Slot enabled and interactive.
three_valued_result.INAPPLICABLE_HERE: Predicate false, but the host can name a single action that would make it true. Slot stays VISIBLE and dimmed; its tooltip states the reason and offers the remedy inline. Example: Node tool on a pixel layer - 'Needs a curve. Convert this pixel layer to curves?' with a button. This is the anti-persona move: instead of hiding a tool behind a mode, show it with the reason and the one-click fix.
three_valued_result.NOT_IN_THIS_DOCUMENT: The tool has no meaning for this document kind at all (Ripple Edit in a print layout). Hidden from the rail. Still returned by search, where it reports why it is absent and what document kind owns it.
three_valued_result.why_three_not_two: Two-valued availability forces a choice between clutter and mystery. The middle state is where discoverability actually lives, and it is the state a persona toggle destroys.

task_scope.definition: A named, document-scoped, temporary FILTER layered on top of the predicate. It narrows the visible tool set and swaps the options bar. It does NOT swap panels, menus, shortcuts or the application chrome, and it always has a visible exit.
task_scope.prior_art: Photoshop ships exactly three: Select and Mask (8 tools, 15 properties), Content-Aware Fill (6 tools, 5 properties), Neural Filters (5 tools). All three are in the captured .kys as taskspace / taskspace-tool / taskspace-property elements.
task_scope.why_this_and_not_persona: A task scope is entered deliberately for one operation on one document, and leaves. A persona is a global state the user must remember they are in. The first is a tool; the second is a mode error waiting to happen.

workspaces_are_ranking_hints.rule: A workspace supplies (a) a rail ordering, (b) a set of pinned groups, (c) a panel layout, and (d) a search ranking bias. It supplies no gate.
workspaces_are_ranking_hints.evidence: All 42 shipped workspaces across Affinity, Illustrator, Premiere and Dreamweaver are job-named. Studio's shipped set should mirror that vocabulary rather than invent one: Photo, Illustrate, Layout, Retouch, Colour, Type, Composite, Motion, Edit, Web, Slice, Catalog.
workspaces_are_ranking_hints.consequence: A user in the Layout workspace who needs the Healing Brush gets it, dimmed-or-enabled according to the predicate, without leaving anything.

two_surfaces_one_rule.rule: If changing the value changes what the tool will DO NEXT, it belongs in the Options Bar. If it changes what is ALREADY on the canvas, it belongs in the Properties panel.
two_surfaces_one_rule.vendor_confirmation: Affinity itself splits these: 802 strings across 146 tools live under context-toolbar contexts (what the tool will do), while 238 [Reflected property] and 177 [Reflectable property] strings describe what the selection is. InDesign's Control panel and Dreamweaver's 60 property inspectors are the second half of the same split.

options_bar.location: Horizontal, full width, pinned directly under the Studio tab strip and above the canvas. One instance, never per-tool floating.
options_bar.why_there: Four of the nine captured applications converge on that exact position (Photoshop options bar, Illustrator control bar, Affinity context toolbar, InDesign control panel). Premiere even ships a command named cmd.toolpanel.wingtip.place_in_options_bar.
contents_order: the tool's declared controls in declared order
options_bar.preset_first: The preset picker is permanent and leftmost. Evidence that this is the common case: 63 Photoshop tool presets, 643 Photoshop brush presets, 455 Affinity brushes, 379 Premiere shipped effect presets, 325 Lumetri looks, 16,994 total Photoshop preset entries. Most sessions never touch a raw parameter.
options_bar.hard_cap: 12 interactive controls. A tool declaring more than 12 renders its top 12 by declared index in the bar and the remainder in the overflow. A tool declaring more than 30 is a Properties-panel citizen and mirrors only its top 3.

properties_panel.location: Dockable, default right edge, tabbed with Layers.
properties_panel.dispatch: Selection-driven, resolved exactly like Dreamweaver: every inspector declares binds_to (layer kind / object kind / node type), a selection_scope (exact | within | inside_lock) and a priority integer; the host picks the highest-priority match and can stack secondary inspectors below it.
properties_panel.why_a_panel_not_a_bar: Premiere's parameter distribution: median 4 per effect, p90 24, max 2,385; 26 effects exceed 50. Lumetri alone is 98 parameters in 18 sections. No horizontal row survives that.

scrub_value_control.principle: ONE widget, ScrubValue, instantiated from a ParamSpec. The same generation argument as tooltips: the numeric behaviour comes from the captured metadata, so nobody types a range twice and the control cannot drift from the reference application.

interaction_contract.hover: Pointer becomes ResizeHorizontal. Rationale is the operator's: a plain number box does not advertise that it is draggable. A second, non-pointer cue is added (a two-pixel gutter tint on hover) for users who suppress pointer-shape changes or use a touch/pen device where there is no hover pointer at all.
interaction_contract.click_without_movement: Movement under 3px within the press enters text edit and selects all. Enter or Tab commits, Escape reverts to the pre-edit value, blur commits.
interaction_contract.press_and_drag: Continuous scrub. Both axes contribute: delta = dx - dy, so right and up both increase. Summing rather than axis-locking means a diagonal drag works and there is no discontinuity when the drag changes direction.
interaction_contract.wheel: Steps by step_default with no click required. The field CONSUMES the wheel event so the surrounding panel does not scroll while the pointer is over a ScrubValue.

modifiers.why_shift_is_coarse: Studio replaces Photoshop, After Effects, Illustrator and Figma. Photoshop and After Effects scrubby sliders use Shift for x10; Figma uses Shift for x10 and Cmd for 0.1. Matching the applications being replaced beats matching Blender and Nuke, which use Shift for FINE and would be the opposite. This conflict is recorded as an open question because the operator flagged the keys as a proposal item.
modifiers.why_alt_is_excluded: Alt is already the duplicate / subtract-from-selection / sample-alternate modifier in every one of the captured applications. Overloading it for step magnitude guarantees collisions inside canvas gestures.
modifiers.mid_drag: Modifier changes are honoured from that instant forward without the value jumping. Implemented by accumulating in VALUE space rather than recomputing from the drag origin.

interaction_contract.sensitivity: step_default = max(10^-precision, soft_range / 200), so one 200px drag traverses the soft range exactly once. Parameters with bounds_unknown fall back to a magnitude-relative step based on the current value.
interaction_contract.clamping: Always to hard_min/hard_max. Approaching a SOFT bound decelerates the drag and parks there; crossing it requires continuing to drag through a short resistance zone, or typing the value. This matters because 378 of the 618 After Effects parameters that declare both bounds (61.2%) have a soft range narrower than the legal one - a control that knows only one range would be wrong more often than right.
interaction_contract.formatting: Rendered at ParamSpec.precision with ParamSpec.unit / display_unit appended. The PERCENT display flag renders a stored 0..1 as 0..100%.
interaction_contract.undo: One entry per gesture. On press, or on the first wheel notch, an undo coalescing scope keyed by author_id opens; every intermediate value updates the document live but writes into the open scope; the scope closes into a single entry on release, or 400ms after the last wheel notch, labelled from display_name. Escape during a drag aborts the scope and restores the pre-drag value.
interaction_contract.double_click: Reset to ParamSpec.default. Free, because defaults are already captured for 980 After Effects parameters, 1,177 Illustrator parameters, 741 Premiere parameters, 84 Lumetri parameters and 140 Photoshop properties.
interaction_contract.secondary_click: Reset to default, copy value, paste value, link/keyframe (where ParamSpec.keyframable), and 'What does this do?' opening the manual anchor.

generated_not_configured.tooltip_is_the_same_spec: The ScrubValue's tooltip renders display_name, the soft range with the hard range in parentheses when they differ, the default, the unit and the modifier hints - all from the identical ParamSpec the control formats from. This is the tooltip/scrub unification: one record feeds the render, the tooltip and the accessible node.

observed_bounds_hazard.rule: bound_provenance == observed means the control does NOT clamp to that bound. It uses the observed range as the SOFT range and leaves the hard range open.
observed_bounds_hazard.why: Affinity's 32 bounded brush parameter tags are observed across 455 shipped presets, not declared. Clamping to an observed maximum would forbid legal values that simply never appear in a shipped preset - a silent, permanent capability loss that no test would catch.

accessibility.agreement_test: For every numeric descriptor, assert format(accessible_value) == rendered_text, and assert that driving the value through AccessKit yields the clamped expectation and exactly one undo entry.

steps: 1. A build-time generator reads the green-room captures and emits studio-ui-descriptors.json keyed by author_id, plus a generated Rust id enum.
2. UI code names an id from that enum. It never types a display string, a range, a unit or a tooltip. A missing id is a COMPILE error, not a runtime blank.
3. Where a capture supplies text, it is used verbatim (with British/American spelling normalised) and tagged provenance.extraction_method = parsed or resolved.
4. Where no capture supplies text, summary is null, the id is written into tooltip-gaps.json, and L1 renders without the sentence. Nothing is invented.
5. Handshake-only elements with no vendor precedent get authored text in the SAME file with extraction_method = handshake_authored, so authored versus derived stays countable.
6. Regeneration is idempotent and diffable: a vendor capture refresh produces a reviewable diff rather than a silent behaviour change.
population_pipeline.why_this_satisfies_the_no_drift_requirem: The UserManual anchor lives in the same record as the tooltip text and the parameter contract. A behaviour change that edits a ParamSpec necessarily touches the record that names its manual anchor, and CI refuses a descriptor whose anchor does not resolve. The manual cannot fall behind the behaviour because they are the same artifact.

ci_gates: Every widget call site's author_id exists in the descriptor set (enforced by the generated enum).
Every descriptor has a non-empty display_name.
Every descriptor's manual_anchor resolves to a real UserManual section.
Every UserManual section is referenced by at least one descriptor (no orphan documentation).
No literal string may reach the tooltip or AccessKit API: the helper signatures accept the id enum, not &str, so this is a type error rather than a lint.
For every kind==param descriptor: hard bounds present OR bounds_unknown explicitly true.
For every kind==param descriptor: format(accessible_value) == rendered_text.
tooltip-gaps.json count does not increase between builds without an explicit waiver.

discoverability.problem_statement: 40,798 capabilities, 353 tools, 14,681 captured parameters, 9,512 presets. A user who does not know a tool's name must still find it in seconds.

one_registry_many_projections.rule: The menu tree, the command palette, the tool rail, tool search and the family browser are five projections of ONE command registry keyed by author_id. Nothing can exist in one surface and be missing from another.

The vendor variants recovered during deduplication become search aliases at zero extra cost, and this is the highest-value reuse of the dedup work.

surfaces.relationship: Studio registers a scoped provider. Studio rows rank first while Studio has focus. A leading sigil restricts scope (one for tools, one for parameters, one for presets) so a power user can bypass ranking entirely.
surfaces.critical_rule: Availability is DISPLAYED, never used to filter. An unavailable tool still appears in results, dimmed, with its reason and its remedy. Filtering by availability would rebuild the persona problem inside the search box - the user would type a correct name and be told it does not exist.

surfaces.relationship: the menu is the complete projection; anything absent from the menu is a registry bug. Whether out-of-context items grey or hide is an open operator decision (recorded in operator-ui-requirements.json).

ranking_rule.rule: Lower tiers only surface when the query has no better match in a higher tier, or when the user opts into deep search with a sigil.
ranking_rule.why: Without this, the query 'brush' returns 643 Photoshop brush presets and 455 Affinity brushes ahead of the Paint Brush tool, and search becomes useless at exactly the moment it is most needed.

discoverability.learn_the_name_affordance: Every search result and every family-browse cell shows the tool's shortcut and its canonical name. Repeated use through search is how a user graduates to the rail and the keyboard, so search must teach rather than merely serve.

accessibility_scheme.why_it_is_load_bearing: Handshake validates GUI work through an out-of-process inspector. A widget the inspector cannot address by a stable name is a widget that cannot be proven to work. This is not a compliance checkbox; it is the test harness's addressing scheme.

author_id_naming.grammar: studio.<surface>.<group>.<element>[.<sub>]  - dotted path, kebab-case within each segment, matching the existing house style seen in shell.chrome.theme-toggle and command-palette.option.<stable_id>
author_id_naming.charset: [a-z0-9-.] only. Lowercase, kebab-case within a dotted path. No spaces, no underscores, no locale text, no vendor branding.
rules: The second-from-left semantic segment is the CANONICAL FAMILY from the deduplication, so an id survives a marketing rename.
An id, once shipped, is never reused and never renamed. A rename adds a new id plus an aliases[] entry on the descriptor; the inspector accepts either.
The id is never derived from widget position, sibling index, label text or any localised string.
The id is the single join key across the descriptor set, the command registry, the shortcut table, the manual anchor map and the AccessKit node.
author_id_naming.cautionary_evidence: Affinity's own workspace containers list 143 four-character tool ids, and its extraction record states plainly that id_to_name_binding is 'unresolved' - 'Human-readable names are NOT stored next to these ids in any shipped resource file: the .NET string tables are keyed by English source text, and the 4CCs appear in the binaries only as compiled 32-bit literals.' Photoshop does the opposite: its .kys binds every tool name to its OSType 4CC in one record, which is why 92 Photoshop tools were recoverable by name and 143 Affinity tool ids were not. Studio must be Photoshop-shaped here: one record carries the id and the name together.

reconciling_two_existing_id_spaces.problem: The codebase has TWO id spaces: AppCommand.stable_id (kebab-case, hs- prefixed, addresses palette rows as command-palette.option.<stable_id>) and author_id (dotted, addresses widgets and is what Argus targets).
reconciling_two_existing_id_spaces.rule: stable_id = 'hs-' + author_id with dots replaced by hyphens. Derived mechanically, never authored twice. studio.tool.draw-path.pen -> hs-studio-tool-draw-path-pen.
reconciling_two_existing_id_spaces.why: One authored identity per element. Two authored ids is the same drift class as two manual surfaces.

author_id_naming.register_into_the_existing_gate: Every Studio author_id is added to accessibility/registry.rs DECLARED_IDENTITIES (fixed node id) or DECLARED_HASHED_AUTHOR_IDS (dynamic-count widgets such as tool rail slots, palette rows and parameter rows). assert_no_unnamed_interactive already panics on an unregistered interactive node, so the gate this proposal needs is enforced the moment Studio widgets are emitted.

keeping_tooltip_and_accessible_descripti.method: Do not synchronise them. Make divergence unrepresentable.
mechanism: accessible_name IS display_name - the same field, read twice, never copied.
accessible_description IS summary - the same field, read twice, never copied.
The tooltip renderer and the AccessKit node builder both take a &UiDescriptor. Neither accepts a string literal; the API does not have that signature.
For numeric controls, the AccessKit value/min/max/step and the rendered text are both formatted from the same ParamSpec, and a test asserts they agree for every param descriptor.
Localisation swaps the descriptor set, not the call sites, so a translated build changes both surfaces together or neither.
keeping_tooltip_and_accessible_descripti.residual_risk: A control whose visible label is drawn by a custom painter rather than by the descriptor could still drift. Mitigation: the painter also takes the descriptor, and the inspector asserts that the accessible name appears in the rendered text of any control that renders a label at all.

This is the RENDER surface; the store is the authority.
usermanual_binding.why_this_changes_the_proposal_for_the_be: The UserManual already has a per-TOOL row type (UserManualToolEntry), a per-anchor row type (UserManualAnchor), a content_hash on every row, a manual_version stamp, a freshness comparator (freshness.rs, MT-204) and a deterministic seed path (seed.rs). The descriptor generator should therefore emit UserManualToolEntry and UserManualAnchor seed rows AS ITS OUTPUT, not a parallel JSON file that has to be reconciled with the manual afterwards. The tooltip descriptor and the manual entry become literally the same generated record: display_name -> name, summary -> description, availability -> expected_input, unavailable_reason -> common_errors, remedy -> recovery_steps, author_id -> anchor_value. 'The manual is updated in the same change as the behaviour' then holds by construction, because there is only one record.

gates.CX-982: HARD_INTERNAL_USER_MANUAL_CURRENCY. [CX-982-002] every change that creates, changes, wires, exposes, deprecates or removes a behaviour, tool, feature, primitive, workflow, command, IPC channel, config key, diagnostic surface or navigation path MUST update the UserManual IN THE SAME implementation change. [CX-982-001] ModelManual identifiers are aliases only - do not create a parallel manual surface.
gates.HBR-MAN-001: evidence user_manual_diff_in_same_commit; bump the version in the same commit. Enforced in THREE places: .GOV/roles_shared/checks/hbr-man-001-paired-diff.mjs, hbr-man-003-scan.mjs, and a Rust-side runtime guard at src/backend/handshake_core/src/atelier/model_manual_merge.rs:913 which fails with 'wired surface diff detected for scope {guard_scope} but MANUAL_VERSION stayed at {}; HBR-MAN-001 requires the bump in the same commit'.
gates.HBR-MAN-003: manual_self_consistency_test - every named surface must exist at the named contract
gates.consequence: A Studio work packet that adds tools without seeding UserManual rows and bumping USER_MANUAL_VERSION will fail a Rust guard at runtime, not merely a governance check. Descriptor generation is therefore not an optimisation; it is the only tractable way to satisfy CX-982 for 353 tools plus 14,681 parameters.

implementation_order_implied: 1. GAP-BIND-AFFINITY extraction pass (changes the generator's shape; do it before writing the generator).
2. Additive: UiTreeNode gains numeric_value / numeric_min / numeric_max / numeric_step / unit in accessibility/snapshot.rs. Prerequisite for any ScrubValue work and for Argus to assert clamping.
3. The descriptor generator + generated id enum + studio-ui-descriptors.json, keyed to the existing DeclaredIdentity registry.
4. One tooltip helper that emits the egui tooltip AND the AccessKit description from one descriptor; register it in accessibility/registry.rs.
5. Extend AppCommand into the UiDescriptor superset; extract symbol_palette::fuzzy_match into command_palette.rs as the shared matcher.
6. ScrubValue on top of ParamSpec, with set_param_clamped as the single write path for pointer, wheel, text, AccessKit and script.
7. Then the palette, the options bar and the properties panel, which are all projections of the above.

NOTE: Steps 2-4 are shared infrastructure that every other Handshake module benefits from, not Studio-specific work. That is the strongest ROI argument in this proposal: the tooltip and accessibility contract fixes an existing product-wide defect (142 unsynchronised tooltips, zero AccessKit descriptions) while unblocking Studio.

risks.risk: Tooltip prose gets hand-written inside UI source files under deadline pressure, because 40% of tools have no recovered sentence and the blank looks like a bug.
risks.why_plausible: It is the path of least resistance and each individual instance looks harmless.
risks.mitigation: Make it a type error: the tooltip helper accepts the generated id enum, not &str. There is no signature that takes a literal. Missing summaries render L1 without a sentence and appear in tooltip-gaps.json, whose count is a CI gate.

risks.risk: hard and soft bounds get collapsed into one range in the first ScrubValue implementation.
risks.why_plausible: Most parameters in the low-quality sources carry only one range, so one field looks sufficient until After Effects data arrives.
risks.evidence: 378 of the 618 After Effects parameters that declare both (61.2%) have a soft range narrower than the legal one; Lumetri's Temperature is hard[-150,150] but ui[-100,100]; Illustrator ships a separate edit_range on 11 controls, 9 of which differ.
risks.mitigation: Both fields exist in ParamSpec from the first commit even where they are equal. A CI check asserts the field pair is present on every numeric descriptor.

risks.risk: Clamping to Affinity's observed brush bounds silently forbids legal parameter values.
risks.why_plausible: The capture presents observed_min / observed_max in the same shape as a declared range, and 32 of 38 tags have them.
risks.mitigation: bound_provenance is a required field. observed never clamps; it only supplies the soft range. Enforced in the ParamSpec constructor, not by convention.

risks.risk: Availability filtering leaks into search, re-creating the persona problem inside the search box.
risks.why_plausible: Filtering unavailable results out looks like a quality improvement and reduces result noise.
risks.consequence: The user types a correct tool name, gets nothing, and concludes Studio does not have the tool. That is strictly worse than the persona toggle, because a persona at least tells you which mode to switch to.
risks.mitigation: Search NEVER filters on availability. It sorts on it and it displays the reason. Asserted by an inspector test that searches for a NOT_IN_THIS_DOCUMENT tool and requires a result row with a reason.

risks.risk: The 353-tool list is treated as complete and frozen.
risks.why_plausible: It is a specific number in a machine-readable artifact, which invites treating it as ground truth.
risks.evidence: Figma and After Effects contributed zero tools because neither palette was captured. Lightroom's 12 are derived, not parsed. Premiere's 39 were decoded from command ids with label:null.
risks.mitigation: undercount_disclosure is carried in the artifact next to the headline number, and OQ-05 puts the decision in front of the operator.

risks.risk: author_ids get generated from widget position or label text because hand-authoring 1,000+ ids is tedious.
risks.why_plausible: Position-derived ids are trivially automatable and appear to work until the first layout change or the first localisation.
risks.evidence: Affinity's own registry admits id_to_name_binding: unresolved because its ids and its names live in different files with no join key. That is the failure state.
risks.mitigation: The generated id enum is the only way to name a widget; ids are reviewed in the same diff as the descriptor. An id that changes between builds without an aliases[] entry fails CI.

risks.risk: 'Tooltips wherever possible' becomes tooltips constantly, and the product feels hostile.
risks.why_plausible: The requirement is stated as coverage; coverage and interruption are easy to conflate.
risks.mitigation: The anti-annoyance rules are part of the proposal, not a later polish pass: suppression during drag, suppression after operation, never covering the described control or the canvas under the cursor, a global off switch, and the Hintline as a zero-interruption channel (599 strings of precedent).

risks.risk: The long-press flyout gets implemented as the primary path because it is what everyone recognises, and the inspector then cannot drive tool-variant selection deterministically.
risks.consequence: Every GUI test that needs a non-default tool becomes flaky, which is a permanent tax on the validation harness Handshake depends on.
risks.mitigation: Untimed path 1 (marker click / secondary click) is the implementation; long-press is an alias added afterwards and is never the only route. The inspector's expand_flyout action targets the untimed path.

risks.risk: Deep search indexes all 40,798 capabilities at tier 1 and buries the 353 tools.
risks.evidence: 9,512 presets and 15,862 option-kind capabilities are in the registry. A query for 'brush' matches 643 Photoshop brush presets and 455 Affinity brushes before it matches the Paint Brush tool.
risks.mitigation: The six-tier ranking rule, with lower tiers reachable only by sigil or by absence of a higher-tier match.

risks.risk: The synonym table used for deduplication merges two tools that are genuinely different, and the merge becomes invisible downstream.
risks.why_plausible: It is the one authored step in an otherwise mechanical pipeline; e.g. Photoshop's Clone Stamp and Affinity's Clone Brush were merged, and Illustrator's Freehand (Pencil) and Photoshop's Pencil were merged although one is vector and one is raster.
risks.mitigation: Every distinct_tools row carries vendor_variants inline, so any merge is visible and reversible from this artifact alone without re-running the extraction.

risks.risk: The workspace mechanism quietly acquires gating power because a job workspace 'obviously' should not show irrelevant tools.
risks.consequence: That is the persona toggle, rebuilt under a different name.
risks.mitigation: The availability rule states the prohibition explicitly and the inspector can assert it: for any workspace W and any tool T, availability_state(T) must be identical with W active and with W inactive.

risks.risk: The undo coalescing scope leaks - a drag that is interrupted by a crash, a modal, or a focus loss leaves an open scope and the next unrelated edit joins it.
risks.mitigation: The scope is owned by the ScrubValue interaction state and closes on any of: pointer release, focus loss, Escape, modal open, or a 400ms idle timer. A test drives each exit path and asserts exactly one undo entry.

risks.risk: Studio adds a fourth tooltip pattern instead of fixing the existing one.
risks.evidence: The crate today has 142 direct Response::on_hover_text calls across 24 files, no shared helper, and NOTHING sets an AccessKit description - tooltip text is currently invisible to Argus. Adding Studio tooltips the same way multiplies an existing defect by the size of the largest module in the product.
risks.mitigation: Land the single descriptor-driven tooltip helper BEFORE any Studio tooltip, and make it the only signature that reaches the tooltip and AccessKit APIs. Migrating the existing 142 call sites is mechanical and is a product-wide win, not Studio scope creep.

risks.risk: ScrubValue ships before UiTreeNode carries numeric metadata, so OUI-008's accessibility clause is unverifiable.
risks.evidence: UiTreeNode is { id, author_id, node_id, role, label, value, disabled, actions, bounds, children }. It has a string value but no numeric min, max, step or unit. argus.set_value exists and would happily set a value that the inspector cannot check the clamp of.
risks.consequence: Every scrub control would pass CX-503D1 by being clickable while its actual numeric contract went untested - the exact class of defect the inspector exists to catch.
risks.mitigation: The additive snapshot change is a hard predecessor of the first ScrubValue microtask, not a follow-up.

risks.risk: A parallel Studio command registry is created because AppCommand lacks the needed fields.
risks.evidence: AppCommand has no category, no shortcut, no manual_anchor, no provenance and no parameter block, and its three const tables are large. Adding a separate STUDIO_COMMANDS registry with a richer type is the low-friction move.
risks.consequence: Two registries means the menu, the palette and the tool rail can disagree, which breaks OUI-006 directly.
risks.mitigation: Widen AppCommand once. The migration touches three const tables and dispatch_palette_action; that is a bounded, one-time cost against a permanent divergence.

risks.risk: A fourth fuzzy matcher is written for Studio tool search.
risks.evidence: command_palette.rs filtering is a plain substring contains with no ranking. A real matcher already exists at code_editor/symbol_palette.rs:167 and its own doc comment designates command_palette.rs as the extraction target for sharing across the three palettes.
risks.mitigation: Studio's tool search is the trigger to perform that already-flagged extraction, not a reason to add a fourth implementation.

risks.risk: Studio author_ids are minted in a new style (snake_case, or a new prefix) and diverge from the existing registry.
risks.evidence: The codebase already mixes dotted (shell.chrome.theme-toggle), prefixed (command-palette.option., manual-topic-) and flat kebab (manual-pane, module-studio) forms. A new module is exactly where a fourth style gets introduced.
risks.mitigation: The grammar in this proposal was revised to match shell.chrome.theme-toggle exactly. All Studio ids register into the existing DECLARED_IDENTITIES / DECLARED_HASHED_AUTHOR_IDS tables, so assert_no_unnamed_interactive enforces them from the first widget.

risks.risk: Studio seeds its manual entries into the DEPRECATED model_manual shim instead of the canonical user_manual store.
risks.evidence: src/backend/handshake_core/src/model_manual/ still compiles, is still #[path]-included by the desktop app, still exports MANUAL_VERSION 1.5.0 and still has a CommandReference type that looks like the right target. The canonical authority is src/backend/handshake_core/src/user_manual/ at USER_MANUAL_VERSION 2.0.4, backed by SurrealDB user_manual_* tables, with model_manual demoted to a deterministic seed input.
risks.consequence: Entries written to the shim would not appear in /usermanual/search, /usermanual/tools or the freshness comparator, so the L2 'what does this do' affordance would resolve to nothing while every governance check passed.
risks.mitigation: Name user_manual/store.rs row types explicitly in the microtask acceptance criteria, and assert through GET /usermanual/tools/:tool_id that a seeded Studio tool is retrievable.

hardest_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Tool-level tooltip prose cannot be generated at the coverage the requirement implies.
hardest_tradeoffs.tension: OUI-007 says tooltip text must be generated from the captures so it cannot drift. But only ONE of the nine captured applications ships per-tool prose at all (Affinity, 212 sentences), and its resource format provides no key that binds a sentence to a tool name. Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, Premiere and Lightroom contribute tool NAMES and KEYSTROKES and nothing else. So the honest generated coverage at the tool level is at most 59.5%, and mechanically bound coverage is 0%.
options: A: author the missing 143+ summaries by hand - violates the generation principle and guarantees drift.
B: ship L1 tips without a sentence where none exists - honest, degrades the feature for ~40% of tools.
C: run the GAP-BIND-AFFINITY extraction pass first, recover the IL-level key->key join, lift bound coverage to ~58%, then apply B to the remainder.
hardest_tradeoffs.recommendation: C then B. Do the extraction pass before writing any tooltip code, because it changes the shape of the descriptor generator. Accept a permanent authored minority and keep it countable via extraction_method = handshake_authored.
hardest_tradeoffs.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Hand-authoring inside UI source files is exactly the drift the requirement exists to prevent, and it is the path of least resistance under deadline.

hardest_tradeoffs.tradeoff: 80 of the 353 tools (22.7%) are tools only because Affinity says so.
hardest_tradeoffs.tension: adjustment_live (36) and filter_live (44) exist because Affinity models every non-destructive adjustment and live filter as a selectable TOOL. Photoshop and Illustrator model the same operations as menu commands and adjustment layers. Keeping them as tools inflates the palette by nearly a quarter and inflates the availability matrix by the same amount; demoting them to commands drops the distinct tool count to 273 and moves 80 rows into the menu and command palette.
options: A: keep them as tools - matches Affinity muscle memory, costs 80 palette entries and 80 availability predicates.
B: demote all to commands - matches Adobe muscle memory and the majority of the captures, but loses the paint-a-live-filter gesture that only Affinity has and that genuinely needs a tool.

C: split on the gesture test - the ones that require a canvas gesture to specify WHERE they apply (adjustment brush, filter brush, tone brush, mask paint, the liquify set) stay tools; the ones that are a parameter dialog applied to a whole layer (Levels, Curves, Posterize, Threshold, Unsharp Mask, the blurs) become commands that create a layer.
hardest_tradeoffs.recommendation: C. The test is whether the operation needs a canvas gesture to say WHERE it applies. That test is mechanical, defensible from the captures, and cuts the 80 to roughly 14 tools plus 66 commands - which lands Studio's palette in the same size band as every reference application instead of a quarter larger than all of them.
hardest_tradeoffs.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Either a palette nearly a quarter larger than any reference application with 80 extra availability predicates to maintain, or the loss of the paint-a-live-filter capability, which is one of the few genuinely differentiated behaviours in the whole green room.

hardest_tradeoffs.tradeoff: The scrub control's numeric contract is only partially recoverable, and the partial data is unevenly trustworthy.
hardest_tradeoffs.tension: OUI-008 wants clamped, precision-correct, unit-correct scrubbing generated from the captures. Quality varies enormously by source: After Effects gives hard AND soft bounds plus precision plus units on 833 parameters, and 61.2% of those have soft bounds that differ from hard. Premiere's broad catalogue carries bounds on only 6.4% of 9,654 rows. Photoshop leaves 79.7% of its numeric properties with no range. Affinity's bounds are OBSERVED across shipped presets, not declared, so clamping to them would silently forbid legal values.
options: A: clamp to whatever bound is available - fastest, and wrong wherever the bound is observed or is a soft UI bound mistaken for a hard one.
B: only clamp where bound_provenance == declared, render everything else unclamped, and file every gap - correct, but ships with a visible minority of unclamped fields.
C: derive missing bounds by inference from the value type and observed data - looks complete and is unfalsifiable, which makes it the most dangerous option.
hardest_tradeoffs.recommendation: B, with hard/soft as separate fields from day one. Collapsing them into one range is the single most likely irreversible mistake here: 378 of 618 After Effects parameters would get the wrong drag range, and retrofitting a second bound after the widget ships means touching every call site.
hardest_tradeoffs.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: A control that cannot reach a legal value, in a professional tool, with no error message - the failure mode users report as 'the slider is broken' and that no unit test detects because the test uses the same wrong bound.
